properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 5:55PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 555 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Villa Grove, or 52 miles north of Alamosa. This thunderstorm was
nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Villa Grove.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 5:33PM MDT until July 27 at 7:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding through narrow canyons and small creeks
caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Canyon Creek into Ouray, CO.

* WHEN...Until 730 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rockslides and mudslides are possible. Avoid traveling and
recreating through the advisory area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 530 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray and Camp Bird.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 5:06PM MDT until July 27 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Park County in central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry creeks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 506 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This may cause small stream flooding. Between 1
and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen in 30 minutes.

- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.0 inch are expected over
the area in the next hour. This additional rain will result in
flooding of low lying areas and small streams.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bailey, Shawnee and Glenisle.

- The North Fork of the South Platte River is seeing the bulk of
the heaviest rain over the last 30 minutes.  Rapid rises in water
levels along the North Fork are expected in the next hour or
more.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 27 at 4:34PM MDT until July 27 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar
is possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter and Cutler Creek drainages and Highway 550.

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and
other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 432 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 27 at 3:30PM MDT until July 27 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Garfield County in west central Colorado...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 330 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain above Roan Creek. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of creeks and streams, county roads.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of South Central Garfield County along Roan
Creek
